stories.headline: A Tyrannosaurus left four footprints in North Dakota
stories.summary: A trackway of four large theropod footprints has been described from the Maastrichtian rocks of the Hell Creek Formation in North Dakota. The prints were most likely made by an adult Tyrannosaurus rex. The study was published by Falkingham and colleagues.

stories.headline: Rome opens its largest fresco and mosaic to visitors
stories.summary: For the first time in centuries, the public can see what is believed to be ancient Rome's largest fresco and mosaic complex. The Painted City fresco and the Great Mosaic were made in the first century C.E. and came to light three decades ago during excavations of the Baths of Trajan. The mosaic measures 33 feet high and 52 feet wide.

stories.headline: A rare wallaby reappears after 50 years
stories.summary: Conservationists working with the Dambimangari Aboriginal Corporation have photographed the nabarlek, a small endangered rock-wallaby, at two sites in Western Australia where it had not been scientifically recorded before. The animal had not been documented anywhere in that remote region for 50 years. It is the only wallaby that keeps replacing its molar teeth throughout its life, rather as a shark does.

stories.headline: An 1894 dime sells for $1.25 million
stories.summary: An 1894-S Barber dime has sold for $1.25 million at auction. Only 24 of the coins were minted in San Francisco in June 1894, and three of those were reserved for assay, leaving a net mintage of 21. Experts know of just nine examples today.
